TeamResponse now embeds full roster[] (player ObjectIds) — convenient for the new wiring but increases payload size for league-level GET /api/teams (12 teams * ~25 ids each). Consider an opt-in ?include=roster query param to keep the list endpoint lean for screens that don't need it (e.g. Standings already gets 12-team data with rosters even though it only renders names + record).

PlayerRoster.tsx detects ObjectId format to switch between live API and mock generator — robust dual-path. However the fallback mock path is no longer reachable from any wired page; consider deleting dead mock-generator code in a follow-up to reduce surface area.
server.py is now ~3940+ lines. Iteration 11-13 already flagged this. Splitting into routers/{auth,leagues,teams,rosters,matchups,live_scoring}.py is overdue.

Matchup.tsx now correctly reads home_team_id/away_team_id, but consider extracting the team-resolution logic (lookup myTeam vs opponentTeam by id) into a small hook — currently duplicated across Matchup/Standings/Roster.
